~
SET UP ALL EXPERIMENTS
~

```{r}
pca.df <- read.csv("pca.df.update copy.csv")
library(phyloseq)

ie.ps.cleaner <- readRDS("CH1_IE_16S_ps.cleaner copy.RDS")
di.ps.cleaner <- readRDS("diel.ps.cleaner copy.rds")
sm.ps.cleaner <- readRDS("sm.ps.cleaner.byrun.rds")

look <- function(ps, name) {
  cat("\n\n==========", name, "==========\n")
  print(ps)                                            # taxa, samples, variables

  cat("\nSample names:\n");      print(sample_names(ps))
  cat("\nMetadata columns:\n");  print(colnames(sample_data(ps)))
  cat("\nTaxonomy columns:\n");  print(colnames(tax_table(ps)))

  cat("\nReads per sample (lowest 5):\n")
  print(head(sort(sample_sums(ps)), 5))
  cat("Read range:", range(sample_sums(ps)), "\n")

  cat("\nASVs with zero reads:", sum(taxa_sums(ps) == 0), "\n")

  cat("\nKingdom counts:\n")
  print(table(tax_table(ps)[, "Kingdom"], useNA = "ifany"))

  cat("\nSamples per group, for each metadata column:\n")
  sd <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))
  for (v in names(sd)) {
    if (length(unique(sd[[v]])) < 20) {
      cat("\n", v, ":\n"); print(table(sd[[v]], useNA = "ifany"))
    }
  }
}

look(ie.ps.cleaner, "Internal/External")
look(di.ps.cleaner, "Diel")
look(sm.ps.cleaner, "Seasonal")
```

Internal/External: (24 samples; 14,135 ASVs, between 39,249 and 177,990 reads/sample)
Diel: (35 samples; 10,910 ASVs, between 64,854 and 230,257 reads/sample)
Seasonal: (75 samples; 20,833 ASVs, between 13,402 and 197,095 reads/sample)

~
Internal/External Set Up
~

```{r}
library(phyloseq); library(tidyverse)

# ---- prune zero ASVs, rename sequence column ----
ie.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ie.ps.cleaner) > 0, ie.ps.cleaner)
tt <- tax_table(ie.ps); colnames(tt)[colnames(tt) == "V8"] <- "Sequence"
tax_table(ie.ps) <- tt
ntaxa(ie.ps)                                   # 14162 - 27 = 14135

# ---- metadata ----
sd <- data.frame(sample_data(ie.ps))
sd$is.neg <- NULL
sd$Sample.Type <- factor(sd$Sample.Type, levels = c("Internal", "External"))
sd$Site        <- factor(sd$Site)
sd$MatID       <- factor(paste(sd$Site, sd$Mat, sep = "_"))   # unique mat ID
sample_data(ie.ps) <- sample_data(sd)

# ---- check the pairing ----
table(sd$MatID, sd$Sample.Type)    # every row should be 1 1
table(sd$Site, sd$Sample.Type)     # 6 6 / 6 6
```

```{r}
sd$Mat[sd$Sample %in% c("D7", "D8")] <- 8
sd$MatID <- factor(paste(sd$Site, sd$Mat, sep = "_"))
sample_data(ie.ps) <- sample_data(sd)

table(sd$MatID, sd$Sample.Type)   # every row should now be 1 1
```

```{r}
samdf.ie <- read.csv("Metadata_CH1_IE copy.csv")

# fix the duplicated mat number
samdf.ie$Mat[samdf.ie$Sample %in% c("D7", "D8")] <- 8

# unique mat ID for the paired design (negative control gets NA)

                         paste(samdf.ie$Site, samdf.ie$Mat, sep = "_"))

# check: every mat should have 1 Internal + 1 External

write.csv(samdf.ie, "Metadata_CH1_IE_v2.csv", row.names = FALSE)
samdf.ie <- samdf.ie[-1, ]
```

Summary: 
- 24 samples
- 14,135 ASVs (14162 - 27 = 14135) ~ 27 0 asvs across all samples (prune_taxa)
- 39,249–177,990 reads per sample.

DIEL Set Up
~
```{r}
library(phyloseq); library(tidyverse)

# ---- prune zero ASVs, rename sequence column ----
di.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(di.ps.cleaner) > 0, di.ps.cleaner)
tt <- tax_table(di.ps); colnames(tt)[colnames(tt) == "V7"] <- "Sequence"
tax_table(di.ps) <- tt
ntaxa(di.ps)                                   # 11007 - 97 = 10910

# ---- metadata ----
sd.di <- data.frame(sample_data(di.ps))
sd.di$is.neg <- NULL
unique(sd.di$Diel_Time)                        # check raw labels before factoring

sd.di$Diel_Time     <- factor(sd.di$Diel_Time, levels = 0:6)   # 7 time points
sd.di$Diel_Time_num <- as.numeric(as.character(sd.di$Diel_Time))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sd.di$Diel_Time))
sample_data(di.ps) <- sample_data(sd.di)

# ---- check the design ----
table(sd.di$Diel_Time)                         # 5 per time point
table(sd.di$Month_Year)                        # all July_2024

View(sd.di)
```

- 10,910 ASVs after removing the 97 with zero reads, which matches the expected 11,007 − 97.
- 7 time points, 0–6. The labels were clean numbers, so they converted to a factor without problems.
- 5 samples at every time point, so the design is fully balanced with 35 samples.
- Independent samples (taken from different mats) 
- All samples are from July 2024, so there's no month effect to account for. 

~
SEASONAL Set Up
~
```{r}
library(phyloseq); library(tidyverse)

# ---- check zero ASVs and taxonomy columns (both already clean) ----
sm.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(sm.ps.cleaner) > 0, sm.ps.cleaner)
ntaxa(sm.ps)                                   # 20833 (no zero ASVs)
colnames(tax_table(sm.ps))                     # Kingdom ... Genus, Sequence

# ---- metadata ----
sd.sm <- data.frame(sample_data(sm.ps))
sd.sm$is.neg <- NULL
sd.sm[] <- lapply(sd.sm, function(x) if (is.character(x)) trimws(x) else x)
unique(sd.sm$Month)                            # check raw labels before factoring

# months in time order
month_order <- c("June_2023", "July_2023", "October_2023", "December_2023",
                 "February_2024", "April_2024", "June_2024", "August_2024",
                 "July_2025")
sd.sm$Month <- factor(sd.sm$Month, levels = month_order)

# season
sd.sm$Season <- case_when(
  grepl("^(June|July|August)", sd.sm$Month) ~ "Summer",
  grepl("^October",            sd.sm$Month) ~ "Fall",
  grepl("^(December|February)", sd.sm$Month) ~ "Winter",
  grepl("^April",              sd.sm$Month) ~ "Spring")
sd.sm$Season <- factor(sd.sm$Season, levels = c("Summer", "Fall", "Winter", "Spring"))

sd.sm$Site <- factor(sd.sm$Site)
sd.sm$Run  <- factor(sd.sm$Run)
sd.sm$NUT[sd.sm$NUT == ""] <- NA               # blanks -> NA

stopifnot(!anyNA(sd.sm$Month), !anyNA(sd.sm$Season))
sample_data(sm.ps) <- sample_data(sd.sm)

# ---- check the design ----
table(sd.sm$Month, sd.sm$Site)                 # samples per month x site
table(sd.sm$Month, sd.sm$Run)                  # Aug 2024 + Jul 2025 = R11002
table(sd.sm$Season, sd.sm$Site)
View(sd.sm)
```

Seasonal: 
- 75 samples
- 20,833 ASVs
- between 13,402 and 197,095 reads/sample
- 9 months (June 2023–July 2025)
- 2 sites.

                 SB TM
  June_2023      0  5
  July_2023      0  5
  October_2023   5  5
  December_2023  4  5
  February_2024  5  5
  April_2024     5  5
  June_2024      5  5
  August_2024    5  5
  July_2025      0  6
               
               
What the design tells you:
- TM is the full time series. It was sampled in all 9 months, almost always with 5 samples (46 total).
- SB was sampled only from October 2023 to August 2024, 6 months ~ All of those months have 5 samples except December, which has 4.
- Both sites were sampled together in only those 6 months. So Site and Month can't both go in one model across all 9 months, because SB is missing June and July 2023 and July 2025.
- Season mostly repeats Month. Fall and spring are one month each, and summer is mostly TM-only months, so the season comparison is lopsided (36 summer samples vs 10 fall). Use Month as the variable tested, and Season only for interpretation/plot colors.

subsetting for seasonal!!!
```{r}
# ---- subset 1: TM time series, all 9 months ----
sm.tm.ps <- subset_samples(sm.ps, Site == "TM")
sm.tm.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(sm.tm.ps) > 0, sm.tm.ps)
sample_data(sm.tm.ps)$Month <- droplevels(sample_data(sm.tm.ps)$Month)
nsamples(sm.tm.ps); ntaxa(sm.tm.ps)            # 46 samples

# ---- subset 2: both sites, Oct 2023 - Aug 2024 ----
both_months <- c("October_2023", "December_2023", "February_2024",
                 "April_2024", "June_2024", "August_2024")
sm.both.ps <- subset_samples(sm.ps, Month %in% both_months)
sm.both.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(sm.both.ps) > 0, sm.both.ps)
sample_data(sm.both.ps)$Month <- droplevels(sample_data(sm.both.ps)$Month)
nsamples(sm.both.ps); ntaxa(sm.both.ps)        # 59 samples
table(sample_data(sm.both.ps)$Month, sample_data(sm.both.ps)$Site)
```
Summary lines~
* sm.tm.ps ~ Seasonal, TM time series: 46 samples; 15,130 ASVs; 9 months
* sm.both.ps ~ Seasonal, two-site comparison: 59 samples; 17,796 ASVs; 6 months × 2 sites


~
CHOOSING TAXONOMIC RANK
~
the percentage of ASVs and the percentage of reads with a name at each taxonomic level:
```{r}
tax_assigned <- function(ps) {
  tt    <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps))
  reads <- taxa_sums(ps)
  ranks <- c("Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus")
  data.frame(
    Rank      = ranks,
    pct_ASVs  = sapply(ranks, function(r) round(100 * mean(!is.na(tt[[r]])), 1)),
    pct_reads = sapply(ranks, function(r) round(100 * sum(reads[!is.na(tt[[r]])]) / sum(reads), 1)),
    row.names = NULL)
}

tax_pct <- bind_rows(
  `Internal/External` = tax_assigned(ie.ps),
  Diel                = tax_assigned(di.ps),
  Seasonal            = tax_assigned(sm.ps),
  .id = "Experiment")

tax_pct
tax_pct |> select(-pct_ASVs) |> pivot_wider(names_from = Rank, values_from = pct_reads)  # reads, side by side
```

```{r}
library(phyloseq); library(tidyverse)

# ---- Class-level data ----
rare_lab  <- "Rare taxa (< 1%)"
unass_lab <- "Unassigned at Class level"

make_class_data <- function(ps, vars, rare_cut = 0.01) {
  keys <- c("Sample", vars, "Class")
  df <- ps %>% tax_glom("Class", NArm = FALSE) %>%
    transform_sample_counts(function(x) x / sum(x)) %>% psmelt()
  df$Class <- ifelse(is.na(df$Class), unass_lab, df$Class)
  df <- df %>% group_by(across(all_of(keys))) %>%
    summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
  if (!is.null(rare_cut)) {
    keep <- df %>% group_by(Class) %>% summarise(m = mean(Abundance)) %>%
      filter(m >= rare_cut) %>% pull(Class)
    df <- df %>% mutate(Class = ifelse(Class %in% keep, Class, rare_lab)) %>%
      group_by(across(all_of(keys))) %>%
      summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
  }
  df
}

bar_data <- list(
  IE = list(rare = make_class_data(ie.ps, c("Site", "Sample.Type", "MatID"), 0.01),
            all  = make_class_data(ie.ps, c("Site", "Sample.Type", "MatID"), NULL)),
  DI = list(rare = make_class_data(di.ps, "Diel_Time", 0.01),
            all  = make_class_data(di.ps, "Diel_Time", NULL)),
  SM = list(rare = make_class_data(sm.ps, c("Site", "Month"), 0.01),
            all  = make_class_data(sm.ps, c("Site", "Month"), NULL)))

# ---- colours, shared across all three experiments ----
distinct_palette <- c(
  "#1f78b4", "#FF69B4", "#33a02c", "#ff7f00", "#984ea3", "#e41a1c",
  "#4ea3d9", "#b07cc6", "#66c2a5", "#a65628", "#f781bf", "#238b45",
  "#6a3d9a", "#e6ab02", "#00a6d6", "#d95f02", "#8c6bb1", "#41ae76",
  "#fb6a4a", "#377eb8", "#cab2d6", "#b15928", "#74c476", "#e7298a",
  "#ffd92f", "#006d2c", "#a6cee3", "#d4b9da", "#ff9933", "#7b3294")
special_colors <- setNames(c("grey70", "darkblue"), c(rare_lab, unass_lab))

kept_taxa <- sort(setdiff(unique(unlist(map(bar_data, ~ .x$rare$Class))), names(special_colors)))
all_taxa  <- sort(setdiff(unique(unlist(map(bar_data, ~ .x$all$Class))),  names(special_colors)))
rest_taxa <- setdiff(all_taxa, kept_taxa)

pal <- rep(distinct_palette, length.out = length(kept_taxa) + length(rest_taxa))
class_cols <- c(setNames(pal, c(kept_taxa, rest_taxa)), special_colors)
if (length(kept_taxa) > length(distinct_palette))
  warning("More than 30 Classes pass 1% – colours repeat in the rare-grouped plots too")

# legend / stack order: alphabetical, then Unassigned, then Rare taxa
order_classes <- function(x) {
  present <- unique(x)
  factor(x, levels = c(sort(setdiff(present, names(special_colors))),
                       intersect(c(unass_lab, rare_lab), present)))
}

nice_lab  <- function(z) gsub("_", " ", z)        # "June_2023" -> "June 2023"
bar_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))

# ---- plot functions ----
# (1) and (2): mean relative abundance per group
plot_mean <- function(df, x, facet = NULL, xlab = x, title, legend_cols = 1) {
  d <- df %>% group_by(across(all_of(c(facet, x, "Class")))) %>%
    summarise(Abundance = mean(Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Class = order_classes(Class))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(.data[[x]], Abundance, fill = Class)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = class_cols) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = nice_lab) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Mean relative abundance", title = title) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = legend_cols)) + bar_theme
  if (!is.null(facet))
    p <- p + facet_grid(reformulate(facet), scales = "free_x", space = "free_x")
  p
}

# (3): every sample its own bar
plot_samples <- function(df, cols, rows = NULL, order_by = NULL, title) {
  if (!is.null(order_by))
    df$Sample <- factor(df$Sample, levels = unique(df$Sample[order(df[[order_by]], df$Sample)]))
  df <- df %>% mutate(Class = order_classes(Class))
  f  <- as.formula(paste(if (is.null(rows)) "." else rows, "~", paste(cols, collapse = " + ")))
  ggplot(df, aes(Sample, Abundance, fill = Class)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.9) +
    facet_grid(f, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x",
               labeller = labeller(.default = function(z) gsub("_", "\n", z))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = class_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative abundance", title = title) +
    bar_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7))
}

# ---- 3 plots per experiment ----
bar_plots <- list(
  IE = list(
    rare    = plot_mean(bar_data$IE$rare, "Sample.Type", facet = "Site", xlab = NULL,
                        title = "Internal/External – Class (rare <1% grouped)"),
    all     = plot_mean(bar_data$IE$all,  "Sample.Type", facet = "Site", xlab = NULL,
                        title = "Internal/External – Class (all taxa)", legend_cols = 3),
    samples = plot_samples(bar_data$IE$rare, cols = c("Site", "Sample.Type"), order_by = "MatID",
                           title = "Internal/External – Class, all samples (rare <1% grouped)")),
  DI = list(
    rare    = plot_mean(bar_data$DI$rare, "Diel_Time", xlab = "Diel time point",
                        title = "Diel – Class (rare <1% grouped)"),
    all     = plot_mean(bar_data$DI$all,  "Diel_Time", xlab = "Diel time point",
                        title = "Diel – Class (all taxa)", legend_cols = 3),
    samples = plot_samples(bar_data$DI$rare, cols = "Diel_Time",
                           title = "Diel – Class, all samples (rare <1% grouped)")),
  SM = list(
    rare    = plot_mean(bar_data$SM$rare, "Month", facet = "Site", xlab = NULL,
                        title = "Seasonal – Class (rare <1% grouped)") +
                theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)),
    all     = plot_mean(bar_data$SM$all,  "Month", facet = "Site", xlab = NULL,
                        title = "Seasonal – Class (all taxa)", legend_cols = 3) +
                theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)),
    samples = plot_samples(bar_data$SM$rare, cols = "Month", rows = "Site",
                           title = "Seasonal – Class, all samples (rare <1% grouped)")))

walk(bar_plots, ~ walk(.x, print))
```

```{r}
# ---- rarefaction curve set up ----
library(phyloseq)
library(vegan)

# helper: counts as samples x ASVs matrix + matching metadata
get_otu <- function(ps) {
  m <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) m <- t(m)
  md <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))[rownames(m), ]
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(md), rownames(m)))
  list(otu = m, meta = md)
}

# one function, used for every experiment
draw_rarecurve <- function(otu, cols, ltys = 1, title,
                           legend_cols, legend_title,
                           legend_ltys = NULL, legend_lty_title = NULL) {
  vegan::rarecurve(otu, step = 1000, col = cols, lty = ltys, lwd = 1.5,
                   label = FALSE,
                   xlab = "Sequencing depth (reads)",
                   ylab = "Observed ASV richness",
                   main = title)
  abline(v = min(rowSums(otu)), col = "grey40", lty = 2)   # lowest sample depth
  legend("bottomright", legend = names(legend_cols), col = legend_cols,
         lty = 1, lwd = 2, cex = 0.8, bty = "n", title = legend_title)
  if (!is.null(legend_ltys))
    legend("right", legend = names(legend_ltys), lty = legend_ltys,
           lwd = 2, cex = 0.8, bty = "n", title = legend_lty_title)
}

# ---- Internal/External: colour = Sample.Type, line type = Site ----
ie <- get_otu(ie.ps)
type_colors <- c("Internal" = "darkorange2", "External" = "steelblue3")
site_ltys   <- c("SB" = 1, "TM" = 3)
ie_cols <- unname(type_colors[as.character(ie$meta$Sample.Type)])
ie_ltys <- unname(site_ltys[as.character(ie$meta$Site)])

# ---- Diel: colour = time point ----
di <- get_otu(di.ps)
diel_colors <- setNames(hcl.colors(7, "Dark 3"), 0:6)
di_cols <- unname(diel_colors[as.character(di$meta$Diel_Time)])

# ---- Seasonal: colour = Month, line type = Site ----
sm <- get_otu(sm.ps)
month_colors <- setNames(hcl.colors(9, "Dark 3"), levels(sm$meta$Month))
sm_cols <- unname(month_colors[as.character(sm$meta$Month)])
sm_ltys <- unname(site_ltys[as.character(sm$meta$Site)])

# lowest depth per experiment (where the dashed line goes)
sapply(list(IE = ie$otu, Diel = di$otu, Seasonal = sm$otu), function(x) min(rowSums(x)))
```

```{r}
# ---- Seasonal ----
sm_plot <- function() draw_rarecurve(sm$otu, sm_cols, sm_ltys,
  title = "Seasonal rarefaction curves",
```

```{r}
draw_rarecurve <- function(otu, cols, ltys = 1, title,
```

```{r}
library(phyloseq); library(tidyverse); library(vegan)
library(lme4); library(lmerTest)        # lmerTest adds p-values to lmer

# ---- helper: four alpha metrics ----
alpha_df <- function(ps) {
  a <- estimate_richness(ps, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson"))
  a$Evenness <- a$Shannon / log(a$Observed)          # Pielou's evenness
  a$Sample <- sample_names(ps)
  a
}

ie_depth <- min(sample_sums(ie.ps)); ie_depth        # 39,249

# ---- 1. unrarefied ----
ie_alpha_unrare <- alpha_df(ie.ps)

# ---- 2. single-draw rarefied ----
ie.rare <- rarefy_even_depth(ie.ps, sample.size = ie_depth, rngseed = 100,
                             replace = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
ie_alpha_rare1 <- alpha_df(ie.rare)

# ---- 3. 100-draw averaged rarefied ----
ie_alpha_rare100 <- map_dfr(1:100, function(i) {
  alpha_df(rarefy_even_depth(ie.ps, sample.size = ie_depth, rngseed = i,
                             replace = FALSE, verbose = FALSE))
}) |>
  group_by(Sample) |>
  summarise(across(c(Observed, Shannon, InvSimpson, Evenness), mean), .groups = "drop")

# ---- add metadata + depth ----
ie_meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ie.ps)) |>
  mutate(Sample = rownames(data.frame(sample_data(ie.ps))),
         Depth  = sample_sums(ie.ps)) |>
  select(Sample, Site, Sample.Type, MatID, Depth)

ie_alpha <- list(unrarefied   = ie_alpha_unrare,
                 rarefied_1   = ie_alpha_rare1,
                 rarefied_100 = ie_alpha_rare100) |>
  map(~ left_join(.x, ie_meta, by = "Sample"))

# ---- does depth differ by Sample.Type or Site? ----
anova(lmer(log(Depth) ~ Sample.Type * Site + (1 | MatID), data = ie_alpha$unrarefied))

# ---- mixed models for every metric x data set ----
metrics <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson", "Evenness")

run_alpha_ie <- function(df) {
  map_dfr(metrics, function(m) {
    mod <- lmer(as.formula(paste(m, "~ Sample.Type * Site + (1 | MatID)")), data = df)
    a   <- as.data.frame(anova(mod))
    data.frame(metric = m, term = rownames(a),
               F = round(a$`F value`, 2), df_den = round(a$DenDF, 1),
               p = round(a$`Pr(>F)`, 4),
               shapiro_p = round(shapiro.test(resid(mod))$p.value, 3),
               singular  = isSingular(mod))
  })
}

ie_alpha_results <- map_dfr(ie_alpha, run_alpha_ie, .id = "dataset")
ie_alpha_results
```

```{r}
ie_alpha_unrare  <- ie_alpha$unrarefied
ie_alpha_rare1   <- ie_alpha$rarefied_1
ie_alpha_rare100 <- ie_alpha$rarefied_100
ie_alpha_unrare  <- ie_alpha$unrarefied   |> rename(OrigDepth = Depth)
ie_alpha_rare1   <- ie_alpha$rarefied_1   |> rename(OrigDepth = Depth) |> mutate(RareDepth = ie_depth)
ie_alpha_rare100 <- ie_alpha$rarefied_100 |> rename(OrigDepth = Depth) |> mutate(RareDepth = ie_depth)
```

```{r}
View(ie_alpha_unrare)
View(ie_alpha_rare1)
View(ie_alpha_rare100)
```

~ INTERNAL/EXTERNAL ALPHA MODELS

*2 predictor variables (site & internal/external - but have to account for the fact that internal and external mats are from the same mat ID)
* switch from anova to a linear mixed model ~ an ANOVA-type model with one extra piece:
- Fixed effects are what you're testing: Site, Sample.Type and their interaction (same as in ANOVA)
- A random effect, (1 | MatID), lets each mat have its own baseline (because mats are not independent). 
  - One mat might be richer overall than another, and the model accounts for that.

```{r}
library(lme4); library(lmerTest); library(car)

# UNRAREFIED 
lmm.ie.unrare <- lmer(Observed ~ Site * Sample.Type + (1 | MatID), data = ie_alpha_unrare)
anova(lmm.ie.unrare)          # F tests with Satterthwaite df (Site ~1,10; Sample.Type ~1,10)

# Assumption checks
qqnorm(resid(lmm.ie.unrare)); qqline(resid(lmm.ie.unrare), col = "red")
shapiro.test(resid(lmm.ie.unrare))
leveneTest(Observed ~ interaction(Site, Sample.Type), data = ie_alpha_unrare)
plot(fitted(lmm.ie.unrare), resid(lmm.ie.unrare), xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

# Effect sizes
effectsize::eta_squared(lmm.ie.unrare, partial = TRUE)
```
Follow up sig observed interaction for unrare
```{r}
library(emmeans)

emm <- emmeans(lmm.ie.unrare, ~ Sample.Type * Site)
emm                                              # model-estimated means for all 4 groups

# Internal vs External at each site (the paired comparison)
pairs(emmeans(lmm.ie.unrare, ~ Sample.Type | Site))

# SB vs TM for each sample type
pairs(emmeans(lmm.ie.unrare, ~ Site | Sample.Type))

# Interaction plot: lines that cross = the interaction
emmip(lmm.ie.unrare, Sample.Type ~ Site, CIs = TRUE) +
  labs(y = "Observed ASV richness (estimated mean)") + theme_classic()
```

shannon transformed to account for normality assumption
```{r}
lmm.ie.expshan <- lmer(exp(Shannon) ~ Site * Sample.Type + (1 | MatID), data = ie_alpha_unrare)
anova(lmm.ie.expshan)
shapiro.test(resid(lmm.ie.expshan))
```
where is evenness higher?
```{r}
library(emmeans)

lmm.ie.even <- lmer(Evenness ~ Site * Sample.Type + (1 | MatID), data = ie_alpha_unrare)

emmeans(lmm.ie.even, ~ Sample.Type)            # estimated mean evenness: Internal vs External
pairs(emmeans(lmm.ie.even, ~ Sample.Type))     # Internal - External difference + p-value

# raw means as a quick sanity check
ie_alpha_unrare |>
  group_by(Sample.Type) |>
  summarise(mean_evenness = mean(Evenness), sd = sd(Evenness), n = n())
```



Unrare Results: 
Observed
- significant interaction (p = 0.037, partial η² = 0.37) 
- this means the internal vs external difference isn't the same at both sites
- so the main effects can't be read on their own
- Assumptions pass
- Follow up results:
  - no sig differences between internal// external areas at each site 
  - no sig differences between internal or external area (across sites)
  - interesting cross pattern seen....

Evenness
- Sample.Type is significant (p = 0.016, partial η² = 0.46, a large effect): evenness differs between internal and external.
- No interaction, so the difference is consistent at both sites. 
- No Site effect
- Assumptions pass

Inv Simpson
- No sig differences
- Assumptions pass

Shannon 
- Assumptions dont pass!
- Shannon diversity was converted to the effective number of species (exp(H'), Hill number q = 1) to meet model assumptions
  - no sig results

I/E ALPHA DIVERSITY CONCLUSIONS (consistent across unrarefied, single-draw rarefied and 100-draw rarefied data)

Observed richness: 
- significant Site × Sample Type interaction (p ≈ 0.04, partial η² ≈ 0.37). 
- The direction of the internal vs external difference reversed between sites: internal locations tended to be richer at SB, and external locations at TM. 
- Neither within-site difference was significant, and SB and TM did not differ for internal or for external samples.

Evenness: 
- differed significantly between internal and external locations (p ≈ 0.02, partial η² ≈ 0.45), consistently at both sites (no interaction). 
- Evenness was higher in internal mat areas. 

~~~~
I/E ALPHA DIVERSITY PLOT

```{r}
library(tidyverse); library(cowplot); library(lme4); library(lmerTest); library(emmeans)

site_cols <- c("SB" = "#1b9e77", "TM" = "#7570b3")
type_cols <- c("Internal" = "pink3", "External" = "steelblue3")

# ---- stats for the labels ----
lmm.ie.even <- lmer(Evenness ~ Site * Sample.Type + (1 | MatID), data = ie_alpha_unrare)
lmm.ie.obs  <- lmer(Observed ~ Site * Sample.Type + (1 | MatID), data = ie_alpha_unrare)

p_type <- anova(lmm.ie.even)["Sample.Type", "Pr(>F)"]               # main effect, evenness
p_int  <- anova(lmm.ie.obs)["Site:Sample.Type", "Pr(>F)"]           # interaction, observed

stars <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "***", ifelse(p < 0.01, "**",
                     ifelse(p < 0.05, "*", paste0("p = ", sprintf("%.2f", p)))))

# within-site Internal vs External contrasts (for the brackets)
even_ct <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans(lmm.ie.even, ~ Sample.Type | Site)))
even_ct$x     <- as.numeric(factor(even_ct$Site, levels = levels(ie_alpha_unrare$Site)))
even_ct$label <- stars(even_ct$p.value)
even_ct                                                          # check these before plotting

y_br  <- max(ie_alpha_unrare$Evenness) + 0.006                   # bracket height
y_top <- y_br + 0.015

# ---- A: Evenness boxplot with site shading + brackets ----
p_even_box <- ggplot(ie_alpha_unrare, aes(Site, Evenness, fill = Sample.Type)) +
  geom_blank() +                                                 # sets up the discrete x axis
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 1.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = site_cols["SB"], alpha = 0.15) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 1.5, xmax = 2.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = site_cols["TM"], alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.6,
               outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.12, dodge.width = 0.8),
             size = 2, alpha = 0.8, shape = 21, colour = "black") +
  # brackets: Internal (x - 0.2) to External (x + 0.2) at each site
  geom_segment(data = even_ct, aes(x = x - 0.2, xend = x + 0.2, y = y_br, yend = y_br),
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(data = even_ct, aes(x = x - 0.2, xend = x - 0.2, y = y_br, yend = y_br - 0.003),
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(data = even_ct, aes(x = x + 0.2, xend = x + 0.2, y = y_br, yend = y_br - 0.003),
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = even_ct, aes(x = x, y = y_br + 0.004, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = type_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.8, y_top), breaks = seq(0.8, 1, 0.05),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Site", y = "Pielou's Evenness", fill = NULL, title = "A",
       subtitle = paste0("Sample type: p = ", sprintf("%.3f", p_type))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)

# ---- B: Observed crossover with interaction label ----
obs_sum <- ie_alpha_unrare |>
  group_by(Site, Sample.Type) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(Observed), se = sd(Observed) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")
dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.15)

p_obs <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = ie_alpha_unrare, aes(Sample.Type, Observed, group = MatID, colour = Site),
            alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = ie_alpha_unrare, aes(Sample.Type, Observed, colour = Site),
             alpha = 0.35, size = 1.5) +
  geom_line(data = obs_sum, aes(Sample.Type, mean, group = Site, colour = Site),
            linewidth = 1.2, position = dodge) +
  geom_errorbar(data = obs_sum, aes(Sample.Type, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se, colour = Site),
                width = 0.08, linewidth = 0.8, position = dodge) +
  geom_point(data = obs_sum, aes(Sample.Type, mean, colour = Site), size = 3.5, position = dodge) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1000, 3500), breaks = seq(1000, 3500, 500),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Observed ASV Richness", colour = "Site", title = "B",
       subtitle = paste0("Site × Sample type: p = ", sprintf("%.3f", p_int))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)

# ---- combine ----
ie_alpha_fig <- plot_grid(p_even_box, p_obs, ncol = 2, align = "h", axis = "tb")
ie_alpha_fig

ggsave("ie_alpha_diversity_fig.pdf", ie_alpha_fig, width = 10, height = 6)
```

~ DIEL ALPHA MODELS
